subject: OpenAI is putting ads inside ChatGPT's images
bodyMarkdown:
OpenAI is about to put ads inside the images ChatGPT draws for you. If you use the free tier, the product you open every day changes this month, and if you hold Google or Meta through an index fund, the forecast that actually matters to you did not move at all.

## What OpenAI announced on Monday

OpenAI said on Monday that it is adding visual display ads to ChatGPT, and TechCrunch reported the same day that the first ones will appear beside the images people ask ChatGPT to generate. The test starts later this month in the United States with an initial group of advertisers. OpenAI says the ads will be clearly labelled and will not influence the answers the model gives. It also said ChatGPT now reaches 1.2 billion people a week, which is the only reason any advertiser takes the call. Ads themselves are not new here. They arrived in February, as text, for logged-in adults on the free tier and the $8 a month Go tier in the United States. What changed on Monday is where they sit. OpenAI is moving them into the part of the product people actually stare at, which is the picture.

## The money says text ads were not enough

CNBC reported at the end of August that ChatGPT's ad business had reached a $1 billion annualized **run rate**, meaning the most recent month's revenue multiplied out over a full year, so roughly $83 million a month. That sounds like a lot until you set it beside the number OpenAI gave its own investors, which was about $2.4 billion of ad revenue for 2026. Six months after launch, at $83 million a month, the company is nowhere close. I read Monday's announcement as the answer to that gap. A text answer gets skimmed in four seconds, and so does an ad sitting next to it. An image gets looked at properly, which is why display advertising has always paid better than a line of blue text. Moving ads into image generation raises the price per impression without putting more of them on the screen.

## The rest of the ad market barely notices

This is the part that gets lost in the articles about ChatGPT eating Google. eMarketer forecasts that ads inside AI chatbots will bring in less than $1 billion in the United States this year, about 3 per cent of all AI-related ad spending, and it expects that share to stay below 8 per cent through 2030. The $32 billion eMarketer sees going to AI advertising in the US in 2026 mostly lands somewhere far more boring. More than 80 per cent of it sits next to AI content, like an ordinary search ad above a Google AI Overview. Google still collects that. Its US ad revenue is forecast to grow 5.6 per cent this year, slower than Amazon at 17.9 per cent and Meta at 14.2 per cent. Slowing growth on a base that large is a genuine problem for Google's story. It is also nowhere near the collapse people keep predicting.

## The takeaway

Watch for the next time OpenAI publishes a number rather than a format, because formats are cheap to announce and revenue is not. If the ad run rate is still sitting near $1 billion when the company next talks about it, the 2026 projection was fiction and every year after it needs rewriting. If you use ChatGPT for free, expect the ads to get harder to ignore before they get easier, because that is where the money points. And if you are watching Google, track whether advertisers actually shift budget out of search, which on eMarketer's numbers they have not.
